content.title: About
content.content: Beef bacon with reduced sodium, cooked and ready to eat, is a pre‑cooked dish that combines tender beef with flavorful bacon. The processing reduces the amount of added salt while preserving taste through herbs and natural flavor enhancers.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bacon gives the dish a distinctive smoky aroma that intensifies when reheated.
Sodium reduction is achieved by using a small amount of sea salt together with aromatic herbs.
Beef is an excellent source of iron, zinc, and vitamin B12.
The cooked product can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or frozen for up to 3 months.
In the United States, similar dishes are often served as quick breakfast or lunch options.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Both beef and bacon provide complete protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: The iron from beef is highly bioavailable and supports normal hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Reduced sodium
items.content: Compared with regular processed meats, this product contains significantly less sodium, which helps maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B6 and B12, which are important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Allergy to beef or bacon
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the meat or processing additives.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Bacon adds saturated fats, so people with high cholesterol should consume the product in moderation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although reduced, the product still contains salt, which may be an issue for strict low‑sodium diets.

items.title: Reheating safety
items.content: When reheating, ensure the internal temperature reaches at least 75 °C to prevent bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat in the microwave (2‑3 minutes) or pan‑fry until lightly crisp. It works well in salads, sandwiches, pasta dishes, or served as a main course with vegetable sides.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in the original packaging for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag for up to 3 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.

bread-pita-wheat-or-cracked-wheat.title: Bread, pita, wheat or cracked wheat

content.title: About
content.content: Bread, pita, whole wheat and cracked wheat are products derived from the wheat grain. Bread and pita are baked from dough, while whole wheat and cracked wheat are used as flour, grains or additives in dishes. They provide carbohydrates, dietary fiber, B‑vitamins and essential minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pita originates from the Mediterranean and Middle East; its characteristic pocket forms when baked at high temperature.
Whole wheat retains the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than refined white wheat.
Cracked wheat (bulgur) is a staple in dishes such as couscous, tabbouleh and various porridges.
Sourdough bread contains natural probiotics that may support digestion.
Wheat is one of the oldest cultivated crops, domesticated over 10,000 years ago.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Wheat products deliver sustained energy through slow‑release glucose.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain bread and cracked wheat provide soluble and insoluble fiber that supports gut health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat supplies thiamine, riboflavin, niacin and folate, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Iron, magnesium, phosphorus and zinc are present in wheat‑based foods, contributing to overall nutrition.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: Fiber and protein in whole‑grain bread help maintain a feeling of fullness longer.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some individuals have wheat allergy or gluten intolerance, which can cause gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White bread and pita can raise blood sugar quickly, which may be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Gluten can trigger celiac disease, an autoimmune condition requiring a strict gluten‑free diet.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Certain breads may contain preservatives, added sugars or trans fats; checking the label is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bread and pita are ideal for sandwiches, dips and as a side to soups. Whole wheat can be used as flour for baking, and cracked wheat works well in porridges, salads, soups or as a grain side dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bread and pita in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or bread box to keep the crust from drying out. Keep whole wheat and cracked wheat in an airtight container in the refrigerator or a dark, cool pantry to prevent mold and preserve flavor.

infant-formula-gerber-good-start-soy-sta.title: Infant formula, Gerber Good Start Soy, Stage 1, powder, made with baby water

content.title: About
content.content: Gerber Good Start Soy is a soy‑based infant formula designed for babies from birth to 6 months (Stage 1). The powder is prepared with specially treated baby water, ensuring a safe and controlled composition. The product contains no cow’s milk and is suitable for infants with lactose intolerance.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula is fortified with DHA and ARA – essential fatty acids for brain and eye development.
Contains prebiotics that support a healthy gut microbiome.
Soy protein provides a complete profile of essential amino acids.
Gerber Good Start Soy has undergone clinical testing to confirm its safety for newborns.
Each 400 g can typically lasts 2–3 weeks when fed daily.

items.title: Supports brain development
items.content: Added DHA and ARA help form neural connections and support visual function.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Soy protein is less allergenic than cow’s milk and is easier for infants to digest.

items.title: Promotes healthy digestion
items.content: Prebiotics encourage growth of beneficial gut bacteria, reducing the risk of constipation.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron helps prevent iron‑deficiency anemia in infants.

items.title: Enriched with vitamins and minerals
items.content: Vitamins A, C, D, E, as well as calcium and zinc, support overall growth and immunity.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some infants may develop an allergic reaction to soy proteins; discontinue use if rash, swelling, or breathing difficulties occur.

items.title: Not a substitute for breastfeeding
items.content: The formula is intended only as a supplement or replacement when breastfeeding is not possible.

items.title: Proper reconstitution required
items.content: Incorrect water‑to‑powder ratios can lead to dehydration or nutrient excess.

items.title: Storage after opening
items.content: Keep the opened container in a dry place and use within 30 days to prevent bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: To prepare one bottle, dissolve 1 level scoop (≈4.5 g) of powder in 30 ml of previously boiled and cooled (to 37 °C) baby water. Mix thoroughly until fully dissolved. Use the prepared feed within 1 hour and do not refrigerate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, tightly reseal the container and use within 30 days. Discard if the formula develops an off‑smell, color change, or unusual taste.

squash-summer-casserole-with-tomato-and-.title: Summer Squash Casserole with Tomato and Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash is a tender vegetable with soft flesh, often used in casseroles. Combined with tomatoes and cheese it creates a flavorful dish suitable for lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Summer squash is rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Tomatoes add lycopene – a powerful antioxidant.
Melted cheese improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins from the squash.
Casseroling retains more nutrients than boiling, thanks to short cooking time at moderate heat.
Squash is easily digestible and suitable for children's meals.

items.title: Supports Vision
items.content: Beta‑carotene from squash converts to vitamin A, essential for eye health.

items.title: Antioxidant Protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and vitamin C from squash help combat free radicals.

items.title: Bone Strength
items.content: Calcium and phosphorus from cheese contribute to bone density.

items.title: Immune Support
items.content: Vitamins A and C, along with zinc in cheese, boost the immune system.

items.title: Digestive Benefits
items.content: Squash fiber promotes healthy bowel movements and satiety.

items.title: Dairy Allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: High Sodium Content
items.content: Salt‑rich cheeses can raise blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Tomato Acidity
items.content: Tomatoes may aggravate heartburn in individuals with high gastric acidity.

items.title: Possible Food Toxins
items.content: Some squash varieties contain low levels of cucurbitacin; they should be thoroughly cleaned before cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the casserole hot, cut into portions. It pairs well with a green salad, boiled rice, or whole‑grain bread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the cooked casserole to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in the oven or microwave before serving.
